title: President Marcos expands school voucher program to kinder, elementary
summary: President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease…

blocks.text: Elementary students in General Trias, Cavite line up during flag ceremony in this file photo from June of this year.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease congestion in public schools.

Signed on Nov. 12, Republic Act 12327, or the Basic Education Voucher Assistance Act, covers private basic education institutions receiving government assistance through vouchers for qualified students, teacher subsidies or other school assistance.

The law extends assistance to Filipino students from middle-middle-income households and below, with priority given to those enrolled in congested public schools, particularly in areas without nearby public schools or institutions offering subjects and electives aligned with their chosen senior high school academic tracks.
“Subject to the availability of funds, the implementation of the provisions in this Act for the kindergarten and elementary levels shall commence in school year 2027-2028,” the law stated.

The Department of Education (DepEd) welcomed the legislation, saying it would provide higher subsidies to low-income families while protecting current beneficiaries of the Educational Service Contracting Scheme and the Senior High School Voucher Program until they complete their basic education.
DepEd also said priority would be given to congested public schools, multi-shift institutions and areas lacking public school options.
“Families will be empowered through a public registry detailing nearby participating private schools, slots and fees,” the department said.

The law also establishes the Bureau of Private Education within DepEd to oversee the supervision, regulation, quality assurance and implementation of government assistance programs involving private education.
The bureau will serve as the department’s focal office for engaging private education stakeholders and supporting participating institutions.

To protect learners and ensure accountability, the law prohibits schools from withholding student records because of delayed government payments and establishes anti-fraud measures, including a centralized system for verifying learner eligibility and school compliance. It also provides whistleblower protection to encourage the reporting of irregularities.
The rules and regulations will be released within 60 days, subject to funding availability.
Funding for the law’s implementation will initially come from DepEd’s current budget and will subsequently be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
The budget will be equitably distributed among all regions, including the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
